intent.raw: Create a research strategy so we develop an infra spec from the beginning with lessons from Lean formalization and every other repository surface. Scrub every part of the repository, fan out, zig zag, allow child fan-outs when a DAG point becomes complex, and look for unmapped ideas beyond schema, taxonomy, reflection tower method, and residue.
intent.objective: Design a governed, path-cited, recursively expandable research route that inventories repository infrastructure knowledge, extracts lessons from Lean formalization, compares project and validation infra examples, discovers missing concepts, and produces the evidence base for a future infra-spec package.
intent.operator_sentence: Recover existing infra, schema, taxonomy, reflection, residue, runtime, observability, deployment, and validation evidence; fan out into bounded lanes; zig-zag each lane through critique; spawn child dispatches when a lane becomes a complex DAG; synthesize only path-cited candidates for infra-spec without promoting them before owner review.

route_menu.context_hint: The selected route is full-surface repository research. It recommends delegated fan-out but does not execute subagents without explicit approval.

items.label: Recursive full-surface fanout
items.description: Scrub every repo zone with role-bound lanes, child-dispatch escalation, critique loops, and parent synthesis.

items.label: Single-pass infra x-ray
items.description: A cheaper sequential x-ray over known infra paths; useful for orientation but too shallow for infra-spec authority.

items.label: Robot-talks infra audit
items.description: Role-bound cross-layer critique focused on contradictions between spec, implementation, runtime, observability, and deployment evidence.

items.label: Task-session execution pack
items.description: Execute the approved research route as bounded work units after the dispatch and strategy are accepted.

technique_overlays.trigger: Infra-spec should reuse the Lean formalization lessons without treating mathematical bridge language as implementation proof.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Every transferred lesson is labeled as theorem-backed, documented research, operational analogy, implementation evidence, or candidate-only residue.

technique_overlays.trigger: The requested fanout may discover complex subgraphs that need their own evidence lanes.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Any child dispatch names parent dispatch id, bounded scope, lane owner, expected receipts, stop condition, and join rule before execution.

technique_overlays.trigger: The operator explicitly asks to find things not already mapped.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Each lane must return at least one negative result, one unmapped candidate, or an explicit explanation of why no net-new candidate survived evidence review.

subagent_strategy.trigger: The target spans Lean theorem research, Arcanum governance, implementation/runtime surfaces, validation repos, project snapshots, generated state, schemas, taxonomies, observability, and deployment examples.
subagent_strategy.explanation: A single reader will overfit to whichever surface is most familiar. Role-bound fanout lets lanes map independent evidence, then zig-zag critique and parent synthesis prevent attractive but unsupported infra-spec concepts from becoming authority.
context: Prior Lean formalization research found stale front-door claims and required separate proof, build, status, relation, and bridge ledgers.
Dispatch-spec validator requires subagent roles to declare owned scope, join policy, authorization, and receipts.
Existing repo memory says schema authority should be YAML-first and validator-backed for new canonical machine-readable artifacts.
Repository organization work already separated canonical source, install/runtime surfaces, generated state, and private/local state.
Existing infra examples are distributed across implementation/domainspec, validation/poker-team, projects/*, research/projects/*, arcanum runtime surfaces, and domainspec-lean-formalization.

roles.purpose: Map every top-level repository zone, classify canonical source versus generated state versus install/runtime copy, and identify infra-relevant owners.
Extract Lean formalization lessons for infra-spec: schema/instance split, reflection tower method, residue typing, counterexample discipline, build-proof-status separation, and bridge demotion rules.
Scrub actual infra artifacts: Docker, compose, Pulumi, Caddy, Prometheus, Grafana, CI, hooks, runtime wrappers, env files, scripts, and operations docs.
Map schema, taxonomy, validation, template, glossary, and status vocabularies; propose YAML-first infra-spec contract axes without over-promoting candidates.
Map observability, receipts, telemetry, reflection, residue ledgers, drift signals, and failure modes that infra-spec must make explicit.
Compare infra/spec patterns across projects and validation repos, including poker-team, whisky-doses, body-war, sonar-loop, GoldenQuill, research/domainspec, and implementation/domainspec.
Look for what has not been mapped: missing infra concepts, contradictions, unowned state, implicit runtime assumptions, stale docs, and dangerous equivalence claims.
Join receipts into the infra-spec research brief, candidate DAG, child-dispatch list, validation ledger, and next-route handoff.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Run the recursive infra-spec research fanout with role-bound lanes, path-cited receipts, child-dispatch escalation, and parent synthesis?
receipt_requirements: Each lane returns concrete paths and line references or explicit unresolved globs for every material claim.
Each lane classifies claims as source-backed, implementation-backed, validation-backed, analogy, candidate, stale, contradiction, or unsupported.
Each lane returns at least one residue item or a negative-result explanation.
Any child-dispatch proposal includes parent dispatch id, scope, roles, inputs, outputs, stop conditions, and join policy.
No lane promotes findings into Inventory, Ontology, glossary, sigil, spell, or infra-spec authority without owner review.

steps.name: Recover prior infra-relevant lessons and dispatch guardrails
stop_conditions: Block any route that treats execution evidence as infra-spec promotion authority.
Flag any Lean-derived concept that is not labeled by evidence type.
Keep this phase read-only except for research artifacts under ops/development.

steps.name: X-ray repository zones and infra evidence surfaces
stop_conditions: Flag any top-level zone with unknown owner or unclear source/generated/install/runtime status.
Stop before moving or deleting files; this is research only.

capability_metadata.note: Real installed native skill beyond the core dispatch capability set; not a freeform/unknown handle.

steps.name: Fan out full repository scrub lanes
stop_conditions: Each lane stops at evidence receipts, not implementation edits.
Escalate to child-dispatch-decision-gate when a lane identifies more than five dependent subquestions or crosses owner boundaries.
Flag any lane that cannot cite concrete paths for its core claims.

steps.name: Decide and register child dispatches for complex DAG nodes
stop_conditions: Block child dispatch execution until the operator approves scope and authorization.
Each approved child route must include parent_dispatch_id=infra-spec-research-strategy-20260603.

capability_metadata.note: Real installed native skill beyond the core dispatch capability set; not a freeform/unknown handle.

steps.name: Zig-zag each lane through critique and repair
convergence_criteria: Each lane separates evidence from interpretation.
Each lane records contradictions and stale claims instead of smoothing them over.
Each lane has at least one validation or demotion action.
stop_conditions: Stop if critique collapses into implementation planning before research validation.
Demote unsupported concepts to residue instead of discarding them.

capability_metadata.note: Real installed native skill beyond the core dispatch capability set; not a freeform/unknown handle.

steps.name: Run candidate infra-spec interpretation tournament
convergence_criteria: Selected interpretation must explain deployment/runtime, observability, schema/taxonomy, validation, ownership, and residue.
Rejected interpretations must be recorded with evidence and failure reason.
The winning concept unit must recombine into a future infra-spec package.
stop_conditions: No concept wins unless it preserves source/runtime/evidence boundaries.
No concept wins solely because it is elegant; it must explain actual repo evidence.

steps.name: Synthesize infra-spec research map and candidate DAG
stop_conditions: Keep all infra-spec contract fields candidate-only until validation and owner review.
Do not create formulae/infra-spec or registry entries in this research route.

steps.name: Validate coverage, evidence, and promotion guardrails
stop_conditions: Block if any candidate concept lacks evidence owner and path.
Flag any uncovered repo zone or unreviewed infra example.
Flag any proposed schema artifact that is not YAML-first and validator-backed.

steps.name: Prepare implementation-readiness handoff
stop_conditions: The handoff may recommend formulae/infra-spec creation, but cannot authorize it by itself.
Any mutation route must start from a validated candidate schema and explicit owner decision.

capability_metadata.note: Real installed native skill beyond the core dispatch capability set; not a freeform/unknown handle.

gates.condition: The route may write only research artifacts under ops/development until implementation is separately approved.
Every material infra-spec candidate must cite concrete repository paths or be marked unresolved residue.
Child dispatches can be proposed by the parent route but not executed until approved.
Any future canonical infra-spec schema must be .schema.yml and validator-backed; legacy JSON examples are evidence only.
Research evidence does not promote Inventory, Ontology, glossary, sigil, spell, or infra-spec authority without owner review.

boundaries.contract: Repository artifacts are cited by path and classified by owner/status; they are not copied into infra-spec authority.
Delegated lanes return receipts, evidence, and residue only; parent synthesis owns integration.
Complex DAG nodes may become child dispatches only after explicit operator approval.
Research can recommend schema axes, but formulae/infra-spec creation requires a separate approved implementation route.

authority.lifecycle: dispatch-spec for route shape; operator for execution approval
authority.execution: future task-session or refine execution after approval
authority.evidence: lane receipts and repository path evidence
authority.memory: memory visibility only through explicit memory-update requests
authority.promotion: future owner-reviewed infra-spec package, not this research route

state_namespaces.write_policy: research artifacts only until implementation approval

promotion_splits.rule: Candidate concepts require synthesis, validation, and owner review before becoming contract fields.
Analogy must be demoted unless supported by implementation/runtime evidence.

promotion_guardrails: Do not promote Inventory from execution evidence.
Do not promote Ontology from research synthesis.
Do not promote glossary, sigil, spell, or infra-spec authority from this dispatch.
Do not treat child-dispatch approval as package promotion approval.
